1: # Architecture Layers
2: 
3: Detailed guide to layer responsibilities and interactions in Flutter apps.
4: 
5: ## Layer Overview
6: 
7: ```
8: ┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
9: │           UI Layer                  │
10: │  ┌────────────┐  ┌─────────────┐ │
11: │  │   Views    │  │ ViewModels  │ │
12: │  └────────────┘  └─────────────┘ │
13: └─────────────────────────────────────┘
14:                   ↓
15: ┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
16: │      Domain Layer (Optional)        │
17: │       ┌─────────────────────┐      │
18: │       │     Use-cases       │      │
19: │       └─────────────────────┘      │
20: └─────────────────────────────────────┘
21:                   ↓
22: ┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
23: │          Data Layer                │
24: │  ┌────────────┐  ┌─────────────┐ │
25: │  │Repositories │  │  Services   │ │
26: │  └────────────┘  └─────────────┘ │
27: └─────────────────────────────────────┘
28: ```
29: 
30: ## UI Layer
31: 
32: Responsibility: Interact with user, display data, receive input.
33: 
34: ### Views
35: **What they do:**
36: - Compose widgets to present data
37: - Handle user interactions (taps, form inputs)
38: - Pass events to ViewModel
39: - Re-render when ViewModel state changes
40: 
41: **What they don't do:**
42: - Business logic
43: - Data transformation
44: - State persistence
45: - API calls
46: 
47: **Logic allowed in Views:**
48: - Simple if-statements for conditional rendering
49: - Animation logic
50: - Layout logic (responsive design, orientation)
51: - Simple routing
52: 
53: ### ViewModels
54: **What they do:**
55: - Transform repository data into UI state
56: - Maintain UI state (survives configuration changes)
57: - Expose commands for user actions
58: - Aggregate data from multiple repositories
59: 
60: **What they don't do:**
61: - Direct UI manipulation
62: - Platform API calls
63: - File I/O
64: - Network requests directly (use repositories)
65: 
66: **State management:**
67: - Use ChangeNotifier for simple apps
68: - Consider Provider, Riverpod, or Bloc for complex apps
69: - Expose state as Streams or ChangeNotifiers
70: - Call Repositories directly for simple flows; introduce Use-cases only when
71:   business logic is complex, reused, or spans multiple Repositories.
72: 
73: ## Domain Layer (Optional)
74: 
75: **Purpose**: Abstract complex business logic from ViewModels.
76: 
77: ### When to add Domain Layer
78: Add when ViewModels have logic that:
79: 1. Merges data from multiple repositories
80: 2. Is exceedingly complex
81: 3. Will be reused by different ViewModels
82: 
83: ### Use-cases
84: **What they do:**
85: - Take data from repositories
86: - Transform for UI layer consumption
87: - Encapsulate reusable business logic
88: 
89: **Relationships:**
90: - Use-cases depend on Repositories
91: - Use-cases and Repositories: many-to-many
92: - ViewModels may depend on Use-cases for complex operations and on Repositories
93:   directly for simple operations.
94: 
95: **Pros:**
96: - Avoid code duplication in ViewModels
97: - Improve testability by separating complex logic
98: - Improve code readability in ViewModels
99: 
100: **Cons:**
101: - Increases complexity
102: - Additional mocks for testing
103: - Adds boilerplate code
104: 
105: **Recommendation**: Add use-cases only when needed. Don't force all data access through use-cases for simple operations.
106: 
107: ## Data Layer
108: 
109: Responsibility: Handle business data and logic.
110: 
111: ### Repositories
112: **What they do:**
113: - Single source of truth for data types
114: - Poll data from Services
115: - Transform raw data into domain models
116: - Handle business logic:
117:   - Caching
118:   - Error handling
119:   - Retry logic
120:   - Data refresh (polling, user-triggered)
121: 
122: **What they don't do:**
123: - Direct UI rendering
124: - Business logic better suited for Domain layer
125: - Direct knowledge of other repositories
126: 
127: **Output:**
128: - Domain models (data classes tailored for app needs)
129: - Exposed as Streams (real-time) or Futures (one-time)
130: 
131: **Relationships:**
132: - Many-to-many with ViewModels
133: - Many-to-many with Services
134: - Should not be aware of each other
135: 
136: ### Services
137: **What they do:**
138: - Wrap external data sources
139: - Expose async response objects (Future, Stream)
140: - Isolate data loading
141: - One service per data source
142: 
143: **What they don't do:**
144: - Hold state (stateless)
145: - Business logic
146: - Data transformation
147: - Caching
148: 
149: **Examples:**
150: - Platform APIs (iOS/Android native)
151: - REST/GraphQL API clients
152: - Local file access
153: - Database access
154: - Platform plugins (geolocation, camera, etc.)
155: 
156: **Relationships:**
157: - Many-to-many with Repositories
158: - Can be shared across the app
159:
